title: Global Static Asset Acceleration for Retail Portals
business: E-commerce retailers serving a geographically dispersed customer base who require fast loading times for product images and static site content.
problem: High latency and increased load on origin servers caused by serving static assets directly from a single regional data center to users globally, resulting in slow page rendering.
solution: Cloud CDN leverages Google's global edge network to cache HTTP content at locations physically closer to the end user, reducing the round-trip time for static asset requests and offloading traffic from the origin.
steps: Configure a global HTTP(S) Load Balancer to act as the entry point for traffic.
Enable Cloud CDN on the backend service associated with the load balancer.
Define cache modes to determine how the CDN handles cache-control headers from the origin.
Verify cache hits by inspecting the 'Age' and 'Via' headers in the HTTP response.
outcome: Improved user experience through reduced latency for static assets and decreased infrastructure strain on the origin server.
limitation: Cloud CDN only caches content that is publicly accessible and cacheable; private or dynamic content requires careful configuration to prevent unauthorized data exposure, which can be checked by auditing cache-control headers.

questions.question: In Global Static Asset Acceleration for Retail Portals, what is the primary benefit of using Cloud CDN?
options: It eliminates the need for a load balancer entirely.
It caches HTTP content at global edge locations to reduce latency.
It automatically converts dynamic content into static files.
It replaces the origin server for all database operations.
questions.explanation: Cloud CDN is specifically designed to cache HTTP content at edge locations to improve delivery speed.
questions.evidence: Cloud CDN leverages Google's global edge network to cache HTTP content at locations physically closer to the end user, reducing the round-trip time for static asset requests and offloading traffic from the origin.

questions.question: In Global Static Asset Acceleration for Retail Portals, what is a key limitation regarding content types?
options: It cannot cache images, only text files.
It only works for users within the same region as the origin.
It only caches publicly accessible content, requiring careful header management.
It requires manual cache invalidation for every single request.
questions.explanation: The documentation notes that only public content should be cached to avoid data exposure.
questions.evidence: Cloud CDN only caches content that is publicly accessible and cacheable; private or dynamic content requires careful configuration to prevent unauthorized data exposure, which can be checked by auditing cache-control headers.
